blocks.content: A bind mount maps a specific, exact path on the host filesystem directly into a container. Unlike a volume, you choose precisely where on the host the data lives, Docker does not manage it for you.

A bind mount connects a real, existing path on your host machine straight into the container's filesystem, any file the container reads or writes at that path is genuinely reading and writing the same file on your host disk.

blocks.alt: A direct, literal mapping between two real filesystem paths

blocks.content: 2. The Classic Use Case: Live Local Development
blocks.text: 2. The Classic Use Case: Live Local Development

blocks.content: Because changes are truly shared in both directions, editing a file on your host machine (in your editor, outside the container) shows up inside the running container immediately, no rebuild, no restart, which is exactly why bind mounts are the standard way to get live code reload during local development.

blocks.alt: An edit on the host is instantly visible inside the container

blocks.content:
docker run -v $(pwd):/app -p 3000:3000 node:18 npm run dev
# Editing files locally is immediately reflected inside the container

blocks.content: Unlike a named volume, where Docker decides where the data actually lives on disk, a bind mount is precisely the host path you specify, giving you full, direct control over its location.

blocks.alt: You decide the exact location, not Docker

blocks.content: That same directness is a limitation for anything meant to be portable: a bind mount pointing at /Users/me/project only makes sense on your specific machine. Move the same command to a different server, and that exact path likely does not exist there at all.

blocks.alt: A path tied to one specific host, not portable to another

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A bind mount maps an exact host path directly into a container, changes are shared instantly and in both directions.
This makes bind mounts ideal for local development (live code reload), but tied to one specific host's filesystem layout, unlike a portable named volume.
